q1.question: What is the typical lead time for custom rubber parts?
q1.answer: Standard lead times range from 2-4 weeks for existing tooling, and 4-6 weeks for new tooling development. Prototype parts can often be delivered within 1-2 weeks using rapid tooling methods.

q2.question: How do I choose the right rubber material for my application?
q2.answer: Material selection depends on temperature range, chemical exposure, mechanical requirements, and application standards and operating conditions. Our material selection guide provides detailed comparison data, or contact our engineering team for recommendations.

q3.question: What tolerance levels can you achieve?
q3.answer: We routinely achieve ISO 3302 Class M1 tolerances (±0.05mm for small parts). Tighter tolerances are possible with specialized tooling and process control - consult our engineering team for feasibility.

q4.question: Do you provide PPAP documentation?
q4.answer: Yes, we provide full PPAP documentation including Level 3 submissions with all supporting data. Our quality management system is IATF 16949 certified, ensuring automotive-grade documentation standards.

q5.question: Can you work with customer-supplied materials?
q5.answer: Yes, we can process customer-supplied materials or source specific grades as required. All materials undergo incoming inspection and verification before use in production.

Weather, dust, moisture, salt exposure and cleaning
Finished gasket or sheet request, material, sample and order quantities
Dimensional, visual and assembly test criteria and required records

sections.heading: Check the dimensional stack-up
sections.body: For a simple flat-section example, compression is 100 × (t − g) / t, where t is free gasket thickness and g is the closed gap. The following drawing values illustrate the calculation. Set the actual compression limits from the joint and functional evaluation.

sections.heading: Compare molded and sheet-cut proposals
sections.body: For a molded gasket, define ribs, contours, parting line, thickness transitions and finish. For a die-cut or sheet-cut proposal, specify the sheet material, thickness, profile, holes and edge quality. Compare quantities and inspection on the same basis. Confirm the actual finished-part or sheet supply route for the drawing; uncured compound supply is a separate purchasing task.

sections.heading: Define the environment and the assembly test
sections.body: Include pressure pulses, support and gap changes with temperature and media. Specify actual insulating oil, saltwater or cleaning exposure where relevant. For an outdoor enclosure, agree climate, dust and water tests on the complete assembly. A compound report and an enclosure IP evaluation address different objects.

sections.heading: Separate electrical and sealing requirements
sections.body: If an EMI gasket is specified, distinguish material resistivity, contact resistance and assembly shielding. Define fixture, frequency, compression and conditions after temperature cycling or other exposure. Confirm the required material and supply option against that specification, with a separate sealing acceptance criterion.

sections.heading: Approve representative samples and order records
sections.body: Agree the sample state, dimensional inspection, surface reference and assembly result. Link material and samples to their lot records. Confirm packaging, inspection scope and changes before repeat supply.

RQ-PG-006.label: Bellows & Boots
RQ-PG-006.title: Custom Rubber Bellows and Protective Boots | RubberQ
RQ-PG-006.description: Define custom rubber bellows and boots with full travel, attachment, space and media requirements. Review material candidates and installed sample tests.
RQ-PG-006.h1: Custom Rubber Bellows and Protective Boots
RQ-PG-006.intro: Review flexible bellows and protective boots for industrial mechanisms. Installed length, travel, surrounding media and attachment details define the geometry and material requirements.

sections.heading: Describe the mechanism and protection task
sections.body: Share the bellows or boot drawing with the moving assembly. State what must be protected and whether the part is a cover or has a pressure-boundary function. Include the motion and the fluid, dust or splash exposure at the actual location.

sections.heading: Provide the full movement envelope
sections.body: A single free length does not describe the installed motion. Supply the positions and attachment details needed to review the folds and surrounding clearance.

table.caption: Inputs for a rubber bellows or boot review
rows: Free and installed length, compressed and extended positions
Lateral offset, angular movement or torsion, and their sequence
Both attachment interfaces, diameters, clamp or retention details
Radial envelope, adjacent parts and clearance throughout travel
Speed, cycles or sequence, dwell and any differential pressure or venting
Media on each side, temperature, dust, cleaning and splash
Drawing features, installed movement and protection criteria
Material reference, sample and order quantities, packaging and records

sections.heading: Select the material against actual exposure
sections.body: For a pump boot or other industrial mechanism, identify the working fluid and the media reaching the outside. Include lubrication, cleaning and hot or cold conditions. Compare identified compounds using the exposure and movement requirements together; the polymer name alone does not determine the proposed part’s function.

links.label: Bellows material, motion and exposure review

sections.heading: Evaluate the sample over the complete travel
sections.body: Agree sample identity, conditioning, attachment and the representative motion sequence. Observe fold contact, interference, end retention and the required protection or leakage result. Define temperature, exposure, cycles and acceptance for the application rather than using a generic service-life figure.
items: Check compressed, extended and offset positions in the actual envelope.
Evaluate the specified media, contamination and interface conditions.
Record findings and approve the drawing, material and inspection basis for repeat supply.

RQ-PG-007.label: Custom Molded Parts
RQ-PG-007.title: Custom Molded Rubber Parts | RubberQ
RQ-PG-007.description: Develop custom molded rubber parts from drawings and service requirements. Review compounds, tooling, critical dimensions, sample approval and batch records.
RQ-PG-007.intro: Turn a drawing or functional requirement into a rubber component development discussion. RubberQ reviews compound selection, geometry, tooling and inspection as a connected manufacturing task.

sections.heading: Connect the drawing to the manufacturing task
sections.body: Bring a current drawing, reference part or functional requirement. RubberQ reviews formulation support, mixing, molding, testing and traceability as a connected project. Describe the purpose of the part and its interfaces so material and geometry decisions address the same requirement.

sections.heading: Prepare the information for an engineering quotation
sections.body: Separate fixed requirements from features that can be discussed. If the drawing is still developing, identify the unresolved dimensions, material requirements and assembly constraints.

table.caption: Inputs for a custom molded rubber part
rows: Drawing revision, 3D file if available, interfaces and reference samples
Media, temperature history, movement, loads and cleaning
Existing compound or required properties and applicable specification
Functional dimensions, datums, surface condition and inspection method
Parting-line constraints, inserts, permitted changes and tooling responsibilities
Sample and production quantities, order pattern, packaging and required records
Sample tests, dimensional report, assembly trial and decision responsibilities

sections.heading: Agree tooling and dimensional acceptance
sections.body: Review the parting line, insert location and finishing needs before the tooling decision. Define mold ownership, maintenance responsibilities and how drawing changes affect samples and approval. A tolerance needs a feature, measurement datum and agreed part condition; include demolding, finishing and conditioning where they affect the result.
items: Mark functional dimensions and the support or datum used for measurement.
Specify acceptable flash, edge condition and insert alignment where relevant.
Measure identified samples in the agreed state before approving repeat production.

sections.heading: Evaluate appearance and function separately
sections.body: For colored parts, provide the color designation and a physical reference where available. Agree the material, surface finish, viewing light and color-difference method before signing a sample; a color code alone is not a universal match criterion. For sleeves, plugs or vibration parts, identify installation, load, motion and the assembly measurement required. Color approval and functional approval need their own criteria.

sections.heading: Carry the approved sample into repeat supply
sections.body: Link the approved drawing, compound, inspection criteria and sample result before confirming recurring orders. Agree required batch identification, release records, packaging and change notifications. If a customer submission is required, define its scope with the order. Tooling cost, development sequence and delivery timing follow the defined project.

RQ-PG-008.label: Diaphragms
RQ-PG-008.title: Custom Rubber Diaphragms | RubberQ
RQ-PG-008.description: Define a rubber diaphragm with clamping geometry, stroke, pressure, media and temperature. Agree material evidence, functional samples and supply records.
RQ-PG-008.intro: Discuss a molded diaphragm around its working movement, fluid exposure and assembly. Share the clamping geometry, stroke and pressure conditions for a material and manufacturing review.

sections.heading: Describe the installed movement
sections.body: Provide the diaphragm drawing and the mating assembly. Identify the clamped area, active geometry, thickness transitions and required stroke. State whether a reinforcement is part of the specification so its material, position and manufacturing route can be reviewed with the rubber.

sections.heading: Prepare a complete diaphragm requirement
sections.body: Include the full operating sequence rather than a pressure limit alone.

table.caption: Inputs for a molded diaphragm enquiry
rows: Drawing revision, thickness profile, active diameter and attachment features
Mating dimensions, edge support, compression and assembly method
Stroke, deflection, frequency or sequence, dwell and return conditions
Differential pressure, direction, pulses and startup or shutdown
Fluid or gas composition, concentrations, cleaning and contact time
Cold start, operating history, peaks and conditioning
Required dimensional, leakage, response and cycle-evaluation criteria
Material reference, sample and order quantity, packaging and records

sections.heading: Separate material exposure, gas transfer and function
sections.body: For gas service, define the actual composition and cold conditions. Permeation through a material and leakage at the clamped interface are different questions. Agree any reinforcement, gas-transfer or cycle requirement for the proposed construction. Material aging and repeated flexing also need distinct evaluation plans.

links.label: Material candidates for the specified exposure

sections.heading: Evaluate representative samples in the assembly
sections.body: Agree sample identity, conditioning, clamping and the pressure or motion sequence. If a response curve matters, define its axes, loading direction and acceptance basis. Compare the required leak, movement and return results with the agreed criteria before sample approval. Retain the approved drawing, material and inspection basis for repeat supply.
items: Confirm dimensions and the installed edge condition.
Evaluate function using the defined pressure, stroke and temperature.
Record the result, approval responsibility and any open changes.

RQ-PG-009.label: Rubber-to-Metal Parts
RQ-PG-009.title: Rubber-to-Metal Bonded Components | RubberQ
RQ-PG-009.description: Review rubber-to-metal parts with metal grade, surface, compound and service loads. Define insert control, adhesion tests, dynamic evaluation and samples.
RQ-PG-009.intro: Review bonded rubber components with attention to the elastomer, metal insert and service load. Share the assembly drawing and loading conditions to discuss a development and inspection route.

sections.heading: Define the rubber, metal and finished interface
sections.body: Share the assembly drawing, rubber requirement and metal insert specification. Identify the bond area, mounting interfaces and functional dimensions. Review the metal grade, surface and supplied state together with the compound and manufacturing requirements.

sections.heading: Prepare the component specification
sections.body: Include the information needed to evaluate both the rubber and its metal interface.

table.caption: Inputs for rubber-to-metal component review
rows: Compound reference, required properties and contacting media
Grade, coating, corrosion requirements and drawing revision
Who supplies it, lot identity, preparation limits and protection before bonding
Bond area, locating features, alignment and dimensional criteria
Direction, compression, shear or tension, preload, frequency, amplitude and load history
Temperature, rubber fluid exposure and metal salt or corrosion exposure
Insert position, adhesion method and component or assembly function
Sample and production quantities, packaging and required records

sections.heading: Separate position inspection from adhesion evaluation
sections.body: Specify the insert’s dimensional location and how it is measured. For adhesion, agree a specimen or representative part, fixture, loading method, conditioning and acceptance criterion. Keep material, surface and process identification with the report. Record where separation occurs and what remains on each surface, as well as the measured result.

sections.heading: Define the dynamic task in the installed system
sections.body: For a robot mechanism or another moving assembly, provide the supported mass, preload, mounting geometry and required load direction. Define frequency, amplitude, temperature and the output needed for the decision. A rebound result, static stiffness and dynamic isolation describe different evaluations.
items: Agree the fixture, loading and sample condition for the dynamic result.
Keep rubber media exposure and metal corrosion requirements separately identified.
Evaluate the required assembly response under its defined mounting and operating conditions.

sections.heading: Use trial evidence to approve repeat supply
sections.body: If an insert shifts during molding, retain its location, cavity, locating features, mold restraints and flow or process records for comparison. Agree the controlled trial and evaluate position and adhesion separately. For repeat orders, confirm the approved metal and rubber references, drawing, inspection basis, surface protection, packaging and lot records.

RQ-PG-010.label: FFKM Replacement Seals
RQ-PG-010.title: FFKM Replacement Seals for Equipment Maintenance | RubberQ
RQ-PG-010.description: Review FFKM replacement seals with the original part reference, drawing, service conditions and validation plan. Discuss sample and supply requirements.
RQ-PG-010.h1: FFKM Replacement Seals for Equipment Maintenance
RQ-PG-010.intro: Assess an FFKM replacement around the seal specification and equipment conditions. Share the existing part reference, dimensions, service chemistry and failure history for a technical review.

sections.heading: Start with the existing seal and its duty
sections.body: A replacement review begins with the original requirement and the reason for changing supply. Share the part drawing or reference sample, the equipment position and the conditions the seal actually encounters. A branded reference helps identify the original part; the replacement candidate needs its own specification and evaluation.

sections.heading: Prepare the comparison inputs
sections.body: Use the same requirement set when comparing candidates. Separate dimensions and installation from material evidence and equipment performance.

table.caption: Information for an FFKM replacement review
rows: Drawing revision, part reference, available dimensions and an unused sample where possible
Existing compound or grade, applicable specification and available reports
Mating geometry, closed gap, assembly method and permitted lubricant
Gas or fluid composition, cleaning sequence and the seal position
Temperature, pressure or vacuum conditions, movement and maintenance history
Photographs, lot identification and the circumstances of wear, leakage or contamination
Required sample tests, equipment trial, acceptance criteria and approval responsibility

sections.heading: Evaluate each requirement with the right evidence
sections.body: Erosion, outgassing, particles, extractable substances and assembly leakage describe different evaluations. Identify which matter to the process and the conditions required for each report. A material-family name or a report from an unrelated compound does not establish the proposed seal’s result.

links.label: Comparing FKM, FFKM, cost and validation

sections.heading: Agree the sample and equipment trial
sections.body: Define what the candidate must demonstrate before regular supply. Keep material and component results linked to the drawing, compound and sample lot.
items: Confirm dimensions, fit and installation on identified samples.
Agree the process exposure and functional evaluation required by the equipment team.
Record the acceptance decision, open requirements and any changes to the approved specification.

sections.heading: Keep maintenance and repeat supply traceable
sections.body: Include the planned order pattern, maintenance context and documentation requirements in the enquiry. Agree compound identification, packaging, lot records and change review for repeat orders. Fit, process performance and service life remain application-specific approval questions. An existing brand reference does not imply brand authorization or OEM approval.

faq.question: Do you guarantee a drop-in replacement?
faq.answer: Fit and performance must be established for the application. We review the specification and agree the validation needed before a supply change.

faq.question: Can I send a Kalrez part reference?
faq.answer: You can include an existing brand and part reference with your specification. Brand references identify the part being reviewed and do not imply affiliation or an approved equivalent.

RQ-PG-011.label: Materials
RQ-PG-011.title: Rubber Materials for Precision Components | RubberQ
RQ-PG-011.description: Choose a rubber material review by compound, exposure and component function. Compare candidate families, test records and the required form of supply.
RQ-PG-011.intro: Compare elastomer families against the medium, temperature, movement and durability requirements of your part. Material selection starts with the application and ends with an agreed compound and validation plan.

sections.heading: Specify the compound and the service
sections.body: A polymer family is the starting point for a material discussion. A purchasing specification also needs the compound grade, physical requirements and evaluation conditions. Identify whether you need finished components or compounded material, then describe the part function and the full operating sequence.

sections.heading: Find the relevant material discussion
sections.body: Use these routes to prepare questions about specific grades and conditions.

Actual oil or mixture, mechanical duty and cold-condition requirements
Material form, molding route, flexibility, contact conditions and surface acceptance
Specified oil, thermal history, mechanical requirements and available grade data

sections.heading: Compare the property the component needs
sections.body: For tear or repeated-load concerns, identify the geometry, notch condition, load path and required test method. For prolonged cold exposure, include hold time, strain state and the motion to evaluate. Keep low-temperature, tensile and assembled-function results with their methods and specimens.

links.label: Read tensile reports with the specimen conditions

sections.heading: Clarify other material and environmental references
sections.body: If the drawing names NR, CR, butyl or another polymer, send the exact grade, duty and requested supply form for review. For recycled-content or degradation information, identify the material, calculation basis or test method and conditions. Evaluate the component’s service requirements alongside that information.

sections.heading: Define the acceptance and supply basis
sections.body: Agree the grade, drawing, hardness scale, relevant properties and inspection conditions for the proposed compound. Keep customer-specific requirements with the approval record. For compound supply, identify delivery form and processing conditions; for finished parts, include geometry, quantity and assembly evaluation.

RQ-PG-012.label: FFKM
RQ-PG-012.title: FFKM Materials for Demanding Sealing Conditions | RubberQ
RQ-PG-012.description: Evaluate FFKM using compound identification, process exposure, seal geometry and sample tests. Define material specifications and approval requirements.
RQ-PG-012.h1: FFKM Materials for Demanding Sealing Conditions
RQ-PG-012.intro: Where service chemistry and temperature challenge other elastomers, FFKM is a candidate family for sealing evaluation. The formulation and actual process conditions determine the testing needed.

sections.heading: Specify the duty before selecting FFKM
sections.body: FFKM identifies a perfluoroelastomer family; a purchasing specification needs an identified compound and part. Describe why the present seal is being reviewed and what the candidate must demonstrate. Compare requirements for chemical exposure, temperature, compression and equipment function without treating one family name as a complete specification.

sections.heading: Build the material and part requirement
sections.body: Use the actual exposure at the seal position, including cleaning and changes between process steps. Record operating limits and excursions separately.

table.caption: Inputs for an FFKM material review
rows: Existing compound or original grade, specification revision and traceable reference
Drawing, cross-section, groove, mating surfaces and installation
Gas or fluid composition, concentrations, cleaning and process sequence
Temperature history, pressure or vacuum, compression and movement
Required erosion, particles, outgassing, extractables or leakage evaluation
Sample identification, test conditions, criteria and responsible equipment team

sections.heading: Separate the evidence for each process concern
sections.body: A plasma exposure result, an outgassing report, an extractables measurement and an assembly leak test answer different questions. Agree which outputs your process requires and the method and sample conditions for each. Compare the proposed compound and part on that basis; evidence for another formulation or process location needs its own relevance review.

links.label: Permeation and leakage as separate tasks

sections.heading: Compare candidates against the same decision
sections.body: Set the required evidence before comparing FFKM with an FKM candidate or an existing branded seal. Include the cost of the part, inspection, qualification and maintenance assumptions in a purchasing comparison. A branded reference identifies an original specification; approval of the candidate still depends on the application.

links.label: Comparing FKM, FFKM, cost and validation

sections.heading: Move from sample evaluation to an agreed supply specification
sections.body: Provide drawing revision, quantity, intended equipment duty and the reports needed with samples. Keep compound, part and sample lot linked through evaluation. Agree approval responsibility, packaging, identification and change review before recurring supply. Formulation support and manufacturing discussion begin with the defined scope; specific test arrangements and material availability are confirmed for the project.

RQ-PG-013.label: FKM
RQ-PG-013.title: FKM Materials for Industrial Seals | RubberQ
RQ-PG-013.description: Specify FKM rubber by compound, fluid exposure, temperature history and seal geometry. Review grade references, sample evidence and supply requirements.
RQ-PG-013.intro: Review FKM compounds for a specified fluid and temperature environment. Chemical compatibility, low-temperature behaviour and compression recovery depend on the formulation and application.

sections.heading: Identify the compound behind the material name
sections.body: FKM is a material-family designation. Viton™ is a Chemours trademark for fluoroelastomers. Use the manufacturer’s grade documentation to identify a branded reference; specify the proposed compound separately. A brand name in an enquiry does not establish RubberQ authorization, availability of every grade or replacement equivalence.

sections.heading: Compare complete specifications
sections.body: Share the existing grade or material callout, the required properties and the actual duty. Polymer grade, cure system and the finished compound all belong in the review. A fluorine-content figure alone is insufficient for approval.

table.caption: Information for an FKM grade and compound review
rows: Full original grade, compound code, specification and document revision
Polymer and cure-system information available for the candidate
Complete oil, fuel, chemical or cleaning fluid and its concentration
Cold start, normal temperature, peaks, dwell and recovery conditions
Drawing, groove, mating surface, compression and motion
Specimen, preparation, cure or post-cure state, method and acceptance limits
Part or compound form, quantity, lot identification and change requirements

sections.heading: Evaluate cold conditions and media together
sections.body: Define the temperature at startup and during motion, not only the highest operating temperature. Provide a specific fuel, process chemical or lubricant rather than a general fluid category. Compare candidate reports under relevant conditions and identify the assembly checks needed.
items: State the sample condition and recovery method for a low-temperature result.
Record fluid composition, exposure time and measured property changes.
Verify the required sealing function in the defined assembly.

sections.heading: Separate material data from part acceptance
sections.body: A specimen report needs its compound identity, method and preparation. A finished seal also needs dimensional, surface and assembly criteria. Agree which compression or retained-force question matters to the duty, and compare results using the same conditions.

links.label: Using an ASTM D2000 material callout

sections.heading: Prepare the sample and purchasing decision
sections.body: Send the drawing revision, material reference, quantity and evaluation requirements. For a candidate change, identify the original requirement and approval responsibility before regular supply. Discuss available compound options and required reports against that scope; agree packaging, lot records and change review with the order.

RQ-PG-014.label: EPDM
RQ-PG-014.title: EPDM Materials for Seals and Gaskets | RubberQ
RQ-PG-014.description: Review EPDM seals and gaskets with the complete fluid, temperature cycle and assembly requirements. Define coolant, steam, weathering and sample evaluations.
RQ-PG-014.h1: EPDM Materials for Seals and Gaskets
RQ-PG-014.intro: Discuss EPDM candidates for the weather, water or formulated-fluid exposure in your assembly. Selection should account for the complete medium, temperature cycle and mechanical requirements.

sections.heading: Define the EPDM compound and the interface
sections.body: Start with the compound reference or required properties, the part drawing and the reason for selection. Describe the installed compression, mating surfaces and movement. A material-family name needs a project specification and identified samples before a purchasing decision.

sections.heading: Record the complete fluid exposure
sections.body: Supply the fluid product, composition and concentration, including additives and assembly lubricant. Coolant, fertilizer solution, water treatment chemicals, urea solution and cleaning agents require their actual exposure conditions.

sections.heading: Treat steam as its own exposure
sections.body: For a steam duty, identify wet or dry conditions, temperature and pressure together, dwell, startup and shutdown, cleaning and installation stress. Define the compound and sample evaluation for that sequence. A dry-air aging result alone does not establish steam service life; agree the evidence for the intended maintenance decision.

sections.heading: Define outdoor aging and the installed joint
sections.body: For an outdoor seal, provide sunlight, ozone, moisture and temperature exposure with the installed strain or compression and any bonded interface. An ozone evaluation needs the concentration, temperature, duration, strain and crack-assessment conditions. Agree both appearance and functional criteria; a material selection is separate from the complete enclosure’s performance.

sections.heading: Specify odor or emissions requirements separately
sections.body: If odor or VOC results matter to the component, provide the customer method, sample state, conditioning, packaging history and acceptance criteria for each evaluation. Identify the actual compound and part tested. An odor observation, a VOC report and a material-property result do not replace one another.

sections.heading: Confirm the part, supply form and sample decision
sections.body: Send the drawing, quantity, packaging and documentation needs. For a sheet or gasket enquiry, define thickness, profile and finished-part requirements so the material and manufacturing route can be discussed. For compound supply, define the receiving process separately. Agree dimensional inspection and assembly approval before repeat orders.

RQ-PG-015.label: HNBR

RQ-PG-015.intro: Evaluate HNBR candidates against the fluid, temperature and repeated mechanical loading of your component. Compound selection and part geometry should be reviewed together.

sections.heading: Identify the HNBR candidate and its task
sections.body: Provide the existing compound or polymer grade, available acrylonitrile-content information and required properties. Explain whether the decision concerns fluid exposure, cold starting, repeated loading, friction or an existing failure. Hydrogenation or one property value alone does not qualify a part for every medium and mechanical duty.

sections.heading: Describe the fluid and operating sequence
sections.body: For oil or a glycol-containing coolant, identify the full product, concentration and additives. Include cleaning, mixing, contact duration and the actual temperature and pressure history.

Identified specimens and parts, method, conditions and acceptance criteria

sections.body: For a pressure-loaded seal, define the pressure cycle, release sequence, extrusion gap and support together with media and temperature. Agree the necessary part and assembly trials. sections.body: Send the drawing revision, quantity, reference material and required evaluation. sections.body: State whether you need a finished seal, another molded part or an uncured compound for your process. Keep the material identity with the drawing and quantity rather than treating all nitrile compounds as interchangeable.

sections.heading: Compare oil exposure with the cold requirement
sections.body: Identify the complete oil, fuel, lubricant or working liquid and the real temperature sequence. If the part contacts wastewater or a cleaning mixture, describe constituents, concentration, contaminants and contact duration.

items: Use identified specimens or representative finished parts.

sections.body: Ask for the properties needed by the part specification and the method used to obtain them. Link results to compound and specimen identification. sections.body: Send drawing revision, material reference, quantity and the concern the samples must resolve. sections.heading: Define appearance and dimensions on the same sample

sections.heading: Describe dry heat, hot water and steam separately
sections.body: State temperature, pressure where relevant, contact time, cleaning and startup or shutdown conditions for the actual medium. sections.body: For a static gasket, define compression, joint geometry, temperature, duration and recovery conditions. sections.heading: Describe the complete service sequence
sections.body: Use the real coolant and cleaning sequence rather than a broad fluid label.

table.caption: Inputs for an EV thermal-management part review
rows: Part number, drawing revision and existing material reference
Mating geometry, groove or joint, gap, compression and surface
Product or specification, mixing ratio, additives and cleaning agents
Cold start, hot operation, peaks, dwell and transitions
Operating pressure changes, pulses, interruptions and flow conditions
Installation, insertion or removal, loading and representative part state
Material, dimensional, leakage and cycle criteria; required reports

sections.heading: Evaluate material and assembly results separately
sections.body: Compare candidate reports using identified compounds, specimens, exposure and methods. A material result needs its test context; the installed component needs its own functional criteria. Define the thermal and pressure cycle, sample conditioning, observations and acceptance decision for the assembly.
items: Review changes after the specified fluid exposure.
Evaluate the cold condition and recovery relevant to the part.
Check leakage and required function in the defined installation and operating sequence.

sections.heading: Agree samples, documentation and repeat supply
sections.body: Identify the sample material, drawing and production basis. Specify the customer submission scope and approval responsibility, including PPAP where requested. Keep the agreed part requirements, lot records, packaging and change review with recurring orders. Begin the enquiry with the drawing and available service information.

RQ-PG-033.label: Humanoid Robotics
RQ-PG-033.title: Rubber Components for Humanoid Robotics | RubberQ
RQ-PG-033.description: Define rubber component requirements for humanoid mechanisms with motion, loading, contact and environmental inputs. Plan samples and assembly evaluation.
RQ-PG-033.intro: Review flexible protection, contact surfaces and bonded components around the movement and loading of your mechanism. Share the drawing and functional requirements for an engineering discussion.

sections.heading: Define the component’s job in the mechanism
sections.body: Start with the drawing and the function at the installation point: flexible protection, a contact surface or a bonded component. Identify the mating parts and the movement the rubber must accommodate. These inputs guide the material and molding discussion before samples are specified.

sections.heading: Describe movement, contact and loading
sections.body: A part’s shape alone does not describe its duty. Include the conditions that determine the sample evaluation.

table.caption: Information for a robotics component review
rows: Drawing revision, function, mating parts and available installation space
Full travel, lateral or angular movement, end positions and fixing points
Supported mass, preload, load direction, frequency and amplitude where relevant
Temperature, lubricant, cleaning agents, dust and other exposure
Counterface, normal force, speed, dwell, contaminants and wear criterion
Required property, measurement method, specimen and conditioning
Sample quantity, assembly trial, acceptance criteria and required records

sections.heading: Review flexible covers and bonded components by function
sections.body: For a flexible cover, check the full motion envelope, attachment and protection requirement together. For a bonded component, distinguish metal position and bond acceptance from the static or dynamic response of the assembly. A damping assessment needs the load and operating range, including the mating structure.

sections.heading: Specify contact surfaces with measurable criteria
sections.body: For a contact pad, identify the handled surface and the task it performs. Agree the test setup for grip, wear and surface transfer under the relevant force, speed and contamination. If an electrical property is required, define its method and conditioning separately. Keep each result associated with the tested compound and geometry.

sections.heading: Connect samples to the assembly trial
sections.body: Choose sample conditions that represent the intended installation. Agree who evaluates the assembly, what constitutes acceptance and how changes are handled. Keep the drawing revision, compound, lot and sample records available when moving to repeat orders.

RQ-PG-034.label: General Industrial
RQ-PG-034.title: Custom Rubber Components for Industrial Equipment | RubberQ
RQ-PG-034.description: Source custom rubber components for industrial equipment with drawing, material and inspection support. Define quantities, samples and repeat-order records.
RQ-PG-034.h1: Custom Rubber Components for Industrial Equipment
RQ-PG-034.intro: Bring a seal, gasket, flexible cover or molded component requirement for review. Material, geometry, production volume and inspection requirements guide the manufacturing route.

sections.heading: Bring a defined component requirement
sections.body: RubberQ combines Japanese formulation support with mixing, molding, in-house testing and ERP traceability in China. For an industrial seal, gasket, flexible cover or bonded component, start with the function and interface. Review the drawing, compound requirements and order profile together to define the manufacturing discussion.

sections.heading: Prepare a package for an engineering quotation
sections.body: Keep requirements identifiable for each part. A sample helps explain a component; include the approved drawing and specification when available.

table.caption: Industrial component quotation inputs
rows: Part number, revision, dimensions, mating geometry and assembly
Existing grade or required properties, actual media, temperature and loads
Sample quantity, order quantity, expected demand and delivery requirements
Critical dimensions, visual criteria, methods and required records
Existing tooling information, ownership requirements and change procedure
Sample approval, material tests and assembly acceptance
Finished components or compound supply, packaging and documentation

sections.heading: Separate the sealing task from the vibration task
sections.body: For a seal exposed to a wash fluid, provide the complete fluid and additives, cleaning sequence and joint conditions. For a vibration component, provide supported mass, preload, frequency range, interfaces and the response or noise criterion. If the equipment needs both, give each component its own drawing and acceptance basis.

sections.heading: Move from quotation to repeat supply
sections.body: For a package containing several parts, list each part number, revision, material and quantity separately. Agree the manufacturing route, sample inspection and the records needed for approval before repeat orders. Link the approved specification to the compound and production lot. Where compound supply is requested, define its delivery form and processing requirements separately from finished-part supply.

sections.heading: Agree production controls
sections.body: Discuss inspection, traceability, change control and the records expected for samples and repeat orders.

sections.heading: Define project responsibilities

RQ-PG-036.label: Engineering Resources
RQ-PG-036.title: Rubber Engineering Resources | RubberQ
RQ-PG-036.description: Use rubber engineering guides for O-ring dimensions, hardness, material compatibility and failure review. Prepare the drawing, test questions and specification.
RQ-PG-036.intro: Find material comparisons, drawing checklists and testing questions for your rubber component project. Use the guidance to prepare a specification and identify what needs application-specific validation.

sections.heading: Material selection
sections.body: Compare polymer families, service media and the questions needed to narrow a compound choice.

sections.heading: Drawing and design
sections.body: Review O-ring dimensions, gasket joints, molding considerations and the information that helps an engineering team evaluate a part.

sections.heading: Testing and troubleshooting
sections.body: Connect a failure observation to the loading, exposure and test conditions. A useful investigation preserves the evidence from the actual component.

RQ-PG-037.label: Standards
RQ-PG-037.title: Rubber Standards and Specification Support | RubberQ
RQ-PG-037.description: Prepare rubber part specifications with complete material callouts, standard editions and acceptance requirements. Link each requested test to its report.
RQ-PG-037.intro: Use standards to make requirements measurable. Identify the applicable edition, test conditions and acceptance criteria alongside your material or part drawing.

sections.heading: Use the complete specification
sections.body: Send the full material callout, including suffixes, the specified edition and any customer additions. Keep the drawing revision with the requirement. For ASTM D2000, the complete designation and supplementary requirements form the discussion; a shortened material label leaves questions for the engineering review.

links.label: Preparing a complete ASTM D2000 callout

sections.heading: Match each reference to the requirement
sections.body: Record material, geometry, test and approval requirements separately so each result can be checked against the right basis.

table.caption: Specification references and the information to identify
rows: Complete callout, edition, suffixes and customer additions
Specified ISO 3601-1 or SAE AS568 reference
Edition, size designation, dimensions and applicable tolerances
Relevant scope, tolerance class, critical features and inspection method
Edition, grade and required inspection conditions
Compound, specimen, conditioning, method and result limits
Sample identity, assembly evaluation, records and decision responsibility

sections.heading: Define flame-test evidence for the actual material
sections.body: For a UL 94 flame classification, identify the requested method and classification, compound, specimen form and thickness, conditioning and report. Check that an available report describes the proposed material and test conditions. Material flame results and the assembled product’s approval have their own acceptance requirements.
items: Put the requested classification in the project specification.
Keep the tested material identity and specimen conditions with the result.
Agree any further part or system evaluation with the customer.

sections.heading: Resolve the purchasing basis before samples
sections.body: Provide the applicable documents and identify which requirements govern when drawing, material callout and customer documents differ. Agree open points, required reports and the sample approval route before quoting or testing against an assumed limit. Keep the approved specification and subsequent changes linked to the supplied part.

RQ-PG-038.label: O-Ring Size Guide
RQ-PG-038.title: O-Ring Size and Drawing Guide | RubberQ
RQ-PG-038.description: Identify O-ring size with inside diameter, cross-section, units and drawing revision. Check the specified size series, groove and material before quoting.
RQ-PG-038.intro: Prepare the dimensions needed for an O-ring review. Record the inside diameter, cross-section, groove and mating-part dimensions together with the service conditions.

sections.heading: Identify dimensions and the size reference
sections.body: Record the inside diameter (ID) and circular cross-section diameter (CS), with units and tolerances. If the drawing uses ISO 3601-1 or SAE AS568, include the complete size designation and specified edition. If the series is unknown, send the drawing or original reference and the measured sample information for review.

sections.heading: Keep the part and installation dimensions together
sections.body: A replacement request needs the size reference and the geometry where the seal works.

table.caption: Dimensions and records for an O-ring request
rows: Part reference, drawing revision and size designation if known
ID, CS, units, tolerances and measurement method
New or used, free or installed, damage and available reference sample
Groove dimensions, mating diameter, gap and tolerances
Stretch, compression direction, assembly and static or moving duty
Specified compound, hardness scale and material requirements
Actual media, temperature, pressure history and quantity

sections.heading: Read a simple dimensional example
sections.body: For an undeformed circular O-ring, the nominal outside diameter is ID + 2 × CS. An illustrative ID of 20.0 mm and CS of 2.0 mm gives 24.0 mm outside diameter. These are assumed dimensions to explain the notation; they do not identify a standard size code, tolerance or approved groove.

sections.heading: Review the groove and material separately
sections.body: Confirm the installed geometry using the actual drawing limits, including compression, stretch and clearance. Keep material selection separate from size identification: a metric dimension or dash number does not specify a compound or brand. A used sample may need comparison with the original drawing before dimensions are agreed.

links.label: Review squeeze, gland fill and tolerances
Prepare the fluid and exposure information

sections.heading: Send the specification for review
sections.body: Include the drawing, size reference, material, quantity and acceptance requirements. Agree sample inspection and assembly evaluation before adopting a replacement. Where dimensions or the reference series are missing, mark them as unknown and identify who will confirm them.

RQ-PG-039.label: Rubber Hardness Guide
RQ-PG-039.title: Rubber Hardness: Specifying a Useful Requirement | RubberQ
RQ-PG-039.description: Specify rubber hardness with the scale, method, specimen and measurement conditions. Compare reports, review storage changes and agree part acceptance.
RQ-PG-039.h1: Rubber Hardness: Specifying a Useful Requirement
RQ-PG-039.intro: Hardness is one part of a rubber specification. Include the scale, method, tolerance and measurement conditions with the functional requirements of the component.

sections.heading: Write a measurable hardness requirement
sections.body: A value such as “70” needs a scale and method before it can be used for acceptance. Identify the drawing requirement, tolerance and specified standard edition. Shore A, Shore D and IRHD results belong with their own methods; a conversion chart does not replace measurement by the required method.

sections.heading: Keep the measurement conditions with the result
sections.body: Agree the specimen and measurement arrangement before comparing supplier and customer reports.

table.caption: Inputs for a rubber hardness specification
rows: Value, scale, tolerance, method and specified edition
Compound grade, batch and processing or sample state
Test piece or finished part, thickness, curvature and support
Preparation, temperature, storage and conditioning history
Measurement locations, reading time and agreed repeat measurements
Instrument identification, calibration records and relevant MSA
Responsible party, reporting format and treatment of differing results

sections.heading: Review a change after storage on a comparable basis
sections.body: Keep the original result, lot identity and storage history with an unused reference sample where available. Repeat measurement with the agreed method and conditioning. Record any change alongside dimensions, appearance and the required function. A changed reading is a reason to investigate the part and measurement conditions.

sections.heading: Connect hardness with the part’s function
sections.body: Agree functional acceptance separately for assembly, flexibility, sealing or dynamic response. A hardness number alone does not establish chemical compatibility, compression recovery or an allowable working strain. Use the identified material and representative geometry for the required checks.

links.label: Separate compression set and stress relaxation

RQ-PG-040.label: Material Compatibility
RQ-PG-040.title: Rubber Material Compatibility: What to Specify | RubberQ
RQ-PG-040.description: Prepare rubber compatibility data with the actual fluid, mixture, exposure sequence and compound. Compare material changes separately from installed function.
RQ-PG-040.h1: Rubber Material Compatibility: What to Specify
RQ-PG-040.intro: Prepare a compatibility review using the exact fluid, concentration, temperature and exposure cycle. Generic family comparisons help narrow a discussion but do not replace compound testing.

sections.heading: Identify the fluid and the compound
sections.body: A compatibility review starts with the actual chemical product and candidate grade. Include mixtures, concentration, additives, contamination and cleaning. A polymer family, solvent polarity label or trade name can help identify a starting point; the comparison needs the complete exposure and compound records.

sections.heading: Build an exposure brief
sections.body: List each medium and each stage of service so the test request represents the component’s duty.

table.caption: Inputs for a rubber compatibility review
rows: Product name, composition or available specification, concentration and additives
Contact side, continuous or intermittent exposure, rinses, cleaning and alternating media
Normal and peak conditions, duration, cycles and recovery
Liquid or gas duty, pressure history and decompression where relevant
Exact compound, sample lot, geometry, processing and initial condition
Agreed mass, volume, hardness, strength, recovery or fluid measurements
Dimensions, leakage or required function, conditions and decision criteria

sections.heading: Compare candidates on a common basis
sections.body: For EPDM/FKM, HNBR/FKM, NBR/FKM or AEM/ACM comparisons, identify the grades and compare reports with matched fluids, conditions and methods. Keep initial and exposed results together. A liquid-immersion result informs a material comparison; the installed seal still needs its own functional evaluation.

links.label: Compare FKM and FFKM evaluation requirements

sections.heading: Include the complete cleaning and pressure history
sections.body: A cleaning cycle can involve several chemicals, rinses and temperature stages. Describe each stage and any steam by its actual temperature, pressure and duration. For gas service, include composition, pressure changes and the required decompression evaluation. Where H2S is involved, keep the customer’s metal-standard requirement separate from the elastomer test protocol.

links.label: Prepare a pressure and exposure investigation

sections.heading: Define what a replacement must preserve
sections.body: For a reference part in polyurethane or PTFE, identify its grade, drawing and reason for the proposed change before comparing a rubber candidate. Agree the properties, dimensions, process and function that require evaluation. Send the available specification and mark unknown inputs for review; sample approval and supply scope can then be defined for the project. For a humid or hot-water environment, include humidity or liquid-contact state, temperature and duration with the exact polymer grade. For a fuel, send the full fuel specification and blend information.

RQ-PG-041.label: Seal Failure Review
RQ-PG-041.title: Rubber Seal Failure: A Practical Review Checklist | RubberQ
RQ-PG-041.description: Prepare a rubber seal failure review with damaged and unused samples, installation records and service history. Define an investigation and validate changes.
RQ-PG-041.h1: Rubber Seal Failure: A Practical Review Checklist
RQ-PG-041.intro: Preserve the failed part and operating history before choosing a replacement. A useful review connects the damage location to assembly, exposure, motion and time in service.

sections.heading: Preserve the part and its history
sections.body: Photograph the installed location and damage before changing the assembly. Keep the returned part, its packaging and an unused comparison part where available. Record the part number, drawing revision, compound and lot. Agree specimen handling and return conditions so the condition being investigated remains identifiable.

sections.heading: Build a record of what happened
sections.body: Describe the sequence from storage and installation to the first observed change.

table.caption: Records for a seal failure investigation
rows: Original drawing, specification, initial inspection and unused sample
Storage, installation, first symptom, service duration and recent changes
Location, orientation, tools, lubricant, tightening sequence and mating surfaces
Complete fluids or gases, cleaning, contamination, temperature and pressure history
Motion, load, preload, speed, cycles and gap or alignment conditions
Photographs with scale and location, leakage or response records and affected quantity
Unaffected locations or lots, retained materials and matched operating records

sections.heading: Use observations to choose the next evidence
sections.body: Record what is visible before selecting a cause. The same feature can have several explanations; these questions organize the investigation.

table.caption: Observed changes and evidence to compare
rows: Damage location, assembly path, tools, groove and movement; include gas-pressure history if relevant
Actual clearance and tolerances, support, compound and temperature-pressure history
Counterface, particles, lubrication, speed, load and repeatable operating conditions
Origin, orientation, strained geometry, load path, thermal, ozone or gas exposure history
Original geometry, installed compression, time, temperature and unloading conditions
As-received samples, packaging, storage, cleaning, residue and untreated comparison
Rubber/plastic or metal/coating pair, contact time, moisture, residues and blank comparisons
Fluid and component identities, exposure, comparison samples and measured functional change
Location, metal preparation and lot, fracture surfaces, loading and assembly records

sections.heading: Keep thermal and gas evaluations distinct
sections.body: For a cold-function concern, retain the relevant material report, including the method and specimen for any glass-transition value, alongside the assembly evaluation. For heat aging, keep exposure and loading history with the sample. For pressurized gas, provide composition, pressure, dwell, temperature and decompression sequence, then agree the compound-specific sample and acceptance protocol.

sections.heading: Connect the investigation with the relevant measurement
sections.body: Choose measurements for the question: a material property, an interface condition or the assembled function. Keep specimen identity, method and conditions with each result. Separate compression-set and force-retention questions, and distinguish material permeation from assembly leakage.

links.label: Compare compression set and stress relaxation

sections.heading: Validate the proposed correction
sections.body: Agree the hypothesis, proposed change, sample identity and test conditions before adopting a new material or geometry. Define the acceptance criteria, assembly trial and responsible decision. Preserve before-and-after records and follow the relevant lots in repeat supply.
